ustva.label: VAT return
ustva.explain: The regular report to the tax office of how much VAT you charged and paid.

euer.label: Annual profit report
euer.explain: A simple yearly statement of income minus expenses that shows your profit for tax.

kleinunternehmer.label: Small business, no VAT
kleinunternehmer.explain: A rule for small businesses that lets you skip charging VAT while your revenue stays under the limit.

skr03.label: Chart of accounts
skr03.explain: The standard list of account numbers that every income and expense is filed under.

eigenbeleg.label: Self-issued receipt
eigenbeleg.explain: A receipt you write yourself when the original is lost or never existed.

eingangsbeleg.label: Received
eingangsbeleg.explain: A bill or receipt from someone else, such as an invoice you pay or have paid.

ausgangsbeleg.label: Sent
ausgangsbeleg.explain: An invoice you issued to a customer.

freiberufler.label: Freelance work
freiberufler.explain: Self-employed work in a profession, such as design, consulting, writing or teaching. Your letter from the tax office says which kind of business you have.

gewerbe.label: A trade
gewerbe.explain: A business that sells goods or services and is registered as a trade, such as a shop, a café or a craft business. Your letter from the tax office says which kind you have.

dauerfristverlaengerung.label: Permanent extension
dauerfristverlaengerung.explain: An approval from the tax office that gives you one more month to file and pay your VAT return.

istVersteuerung.label: When my customer pays
istVersteuerung.explain: You owe the VAT for a sale once your customer has paid you, not when you send the invoice.

sollVersteuerung.label: When I send the invoice
sollVersteuerung.explain: You owe the VAT for a sale in the month you send the invoice, even if your customer pays later.

steuernummer.label: Tax number
steuernummer.explain: The number your tax office gave your business. You find it at the top of its letters.

ustIdNr.label: VAT ID
ustIdNr.explain: The EU ID number for VAT. It starts with DE and has nine digits. You only have one if you applied for it, so you can leave it empty.

finanzamt.label: Tax office
finanzamt.explain: The local office that handles your taxes. Its name is on its letters.

umsatzsteuer.label: VAT you charged
umsatzsteuer.explain: The VAT you added to your invoices to customers. You pass it on to the tax office, minus the VAT you paid yourself.

vorsteuer.label: VAT you paid
vorsteuer.explain: The VAT in the bills you paid for your business. You subtract it from the VAT you charged.

elster.label: Online tax filing
elster.explain: ELSTER is the tax office's official online channel. What you send through it arrives there directly.

einkommensteuererklaerung.label: Income tax return
einkommensteuererklaerung.explain: Your personal yearly tax return. It lists all your taxable income, including the profit of your business.

feststellungserklaerung.label: Partnership profit return
feststellungserklaerung.explain: The return of a partnership such as a GbR. It shows the profit of the business and how it is shared between the partners, who each report their share in their own income tax return.

umsatzsteuererklaerung.label: Annual VAT return
umsatzsteuererklaerung.explain: The yearly summary of all your VAT, filed after the monthly or quarterly returns.

uebertragungsprotokoll.label: Transfer receipt
uebertragungsprotokoll.explain: The record that your return was sent to the tax office, with the transfer ticket as proof.

rechnung.label: Invoice
rechnung.explain: The bill you send to a customer. In Germany it has to show both addresses, a running number, the date, what you did and when, and the amount with its VAT.

stornorechnung.label: Cancellation invoice
stornorechnung.explain: A sent invoice may not be changed. You cancel it with a cancellation invoice that repeats it with negative amounts. The original stays on record.

eRechnung.label: E-invoice
eRechnung.explain: An invoice that carries its data in a form a computer can read. Businesses in Germany must be able to receive one, and sending one becomes required step by step.

zugferd.label: PDF with data inside
zugferd.explain: An e-invoice that looks and opens like a normal PDF, with the readable data inside it. It is the usual format for business customers in Germany.

xrechnung.label: Data file for public offices
xrechnung.explain: An e-invoice as a pure data file. Public offices in Germany require it, together with their routing number (Leitweg-ID).

zahlungserinnerung.label: Friendly reminder
zahlungserinnerung.explain: A polite first nudge for an invoice that was not paid by its due date. It adds no fees and gives your customer a week to pay.

mahnung.label: Formal reminder
mahnung.explain: A firmer second reminder, sent after the friendly one. It sets a new date to pay by and says that late-payment interest may be charged. The app does not work out any interest or fees.

leitwegId.label: Routing ID for public offices
leitwegId.explain: The routing number a public office gives you so it can receive your invoice. Without it, the office cannot take the invoice.

reverseCharge.label: Reverse charge
reverseCharge.explain: For a business customer in another EU country, you do not charge German VAT. Your customer pays the VAT in their own country, and the invoice says so.

einzelunternehmen.label: Sole trader
einzelunternehmen.explain: A business owned and run by one person. You and the business are the same in law, so you are liable with everything you own.

gbr.label: Partnership
gbr.explain: A partnership of two or more people who run a business together without registering a company. All partners are liable for its debts.

avv.label: Data processing agreement
avv.explain: The Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag: a contract that data protection law requires when one company handles personal data for another. It sets out what may be done with the data and how it is kept safe.

steuerberater.label: Tax advisor
steuerberater.explain: A licensed professional in Germany who advises on taxes and files tax returns for others. This app does not give personal tax advice; a Steuerberater:in does.
